target_customer: Content creators and consumers who want fast AI image and video generation (B-roll, music visuals, character art)
problem: Generative image and video tools made users wait on long GPU jobs, which slowed creative iteration.
business_model: Consumer freemium subscription with credits, starting near $9.99 a month per third-party reviews
product_category: Consumer generative AI image and video app

founders.name: Rishi Bhuta
founders.background_notes: The launch post says the founders met at Amazon Robotics; whether Bhuta worked there was not separately confirmed.

founders.name: Will Stith
founders.background_notes: Did greenfield R&D in Robotics and Project Kuiper at Amazon, per YC page.

technical_complexity.rationale: Real-time generation required optimized inference of diffusion models; common open models were available in 2023, so the hard part was serving speed rather than research.

defensibility.rationale: Built on widely available generative models, with fast follow competition and little data or network lock-in.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No dated source found on specific moves; the product persists as a small app with a thin public footprint.

market_need_then: Early 2023 saw explosive interest in generative AI imagery and complaints about slow generation, per the company's pitch of avoiding long GPU waits. No traction numbers found.

branding.domain_note: decohere.ai now redirects to decohere.co; the site footer credits Decoherence, Co., suggesting the legal or earlier name Decoherence.

identity.voice_and_tone: Confident and promotional: 'World's fastest AI generator', 'The new age of AI generated content starts here'.

rebrands.why: Not sourced; some directories use Decoherence and Decohere interchangeably.

brand_strength.rationale: Little press and no community evidence; name sounds like Cohere and Decoherence and is easy to confuse.

pivots.from: Real-time generative AI infrastructure and product
pivots.to: Consumer AI generator app with many use-case pages (anime, headshots, D&D art)
pivots.why: Not stated; inferred from YC description versus the current site.

outcome_analysis: Decohere is a four person Seattle team from W23 whose founders met at Amazon Robotics. It positioned on real-time generative image and video, and now runs a consumer freemium generator with SEO style use-case pages. No funding round beyond aggregator figures, no exit and no shutdown news were found, so its trajectory is unclear. Low defensibility and heavy competition are the main risks.
notes: Funding unverified: CB Insights and VCBacked list about $500K across rounds with Unpopular Ventures and Y Combinator, dated April 2023 as seed or pre-seed; these are aggregators that may share a source, so no round is recorded. VCBacked describes a San Francisco Decoherence, possibly a different record. Competitor search returned only current review pages (Artbreeder named without date), so the list is empty. Outcome search found no acquisition, shutdown or layoffs.
